reviews.scope: Probability as a likelihood measure in [0,1]
reviews.reason: A length, area or volume ratio is meaningful as a probability only if the learner already knows probability measures likelihood in [0,1]. The uniform model also extends the equally likely idea to a continuum.

reviews.scope: Solving cut-position inequalities for favorable segment intervals
reviews.reason: In string-cut problems, conditions on piece lengths become linear inequalities in the cut position, and solving them gives the favorable interval. Area and volume models, and direct geometric reasoning, need no such solving.
reviews.counterexample: Mark the favorable subsegment on a diagram by measuring distances from the endpoints, with no symbolic inequality solving.

reviews.scope: Volume probability for nested or disjoint spherical regions
reviews.reason: When the favorable and total regions are spheres, the volume ratio follows from the cube of the radius ratio, which is exactly this node's criterion. Segment, planar and non-spherical solid models never use it.
reviews.counterexample: Uniform probability on a segment or in a planar disk uses length or area ratios only.

reviews.scope: Meaning of the sine and cosine values being inverted
reviews.reason: Arcsin and arccos are defined as the angle whose sine or cosine equals t. Without the forward definitions, the defining condition and the composition checks in the criteria have no meaning.

reviews.scope: Why restricting the domain permits a single-valued inverse
reviews.reason: The general bijection idea explains why the principal range is restricted and why inverse notation differs from a reciprocal. The branch definitions can still be stated directly, and affine inverse procedures play no role.
reviews.counterexample: Define arcsin t directly as the unique angle in [-pi/2,pi/2] with sine t, using unit-circle reasoning only.

reviews.scope: Uniqueness of the arcsin value on its principal interval
reviews.reason: Strict increase of sine on [-pi/2,pi/2] justifies uniqueness of the arcsin angle. Uniqueness can also be read from the unit circle, and arccos rests on cosine behavior on [0,pi] instead.
reviews.counterexample: On the unit circle, only one point in the right half has a given height, so uniqueness follows without monotonicity analysis.

reviews.scope: Parallel principal-branch conventions among inverse trigonometric functions
reviews.reason: Arctan and arcsin/arccos share the idea of restricting the domain to get a principal value, but neither is logically needed for the other. Comparing them helps, but imposes no learning order.
reviews.counterexample: Arcsin and arccos can be mastered fully before tangent inverses are introduced.

reviews.scope: Building the initial finite possible-world set
reviews.reason: Translating static conditions into a set of candidate assignments helps build the initial worlds. The new core skill, recomputing observation classes after announcements, is distinct, and many tasks supply the world list.
reviews.counterexample: A task that lists all possible worlds explicitly needs only class formation and announcement updates.

reviews.scope: Enumerating increasing positive integer triples as initial worlds
reviews.reason: In card tasks with numeric constraints, the initial worlds are the integer solutions under bounds, found by finite Diophantine enumeration. Knowledge-update reasoning itself never needs integer equation solving.
reviews.counterexample: Tasks with dates, colors or supplied world tables have no integer equations to solve.

reviews.scope: Exhaustive enumeration of order and equality score worlds
reviews.reason: Listing every relative-score assignment that meets the order and equality constraints is the finite-deduction route to observation classes. A symbolic counterexample argument can refute knowledge without full enumeration. This complements the general prepares edge.
reviews.counterexample: Show that two specific indistinguishable worlds differ on the proposition, which refutes knowledge without listing every assignment.
